modules.title: Accounting Trail
text: Six Stages of the Accounting Trail
Journal Entry: Chronologically recording transactions in the Journal (Book of Original Entry) with debit and credit details.
Six Stages of the Accounting Trail
Ledger Posting: Transferring journalised details into respective individual accounts within the Ledger (Book of Final Entry).
Six Stages of the Accounting Trail
Trial Balance: Compiling all ledger balances to verify the arithmetical equality of debits and credits.
Six Stages of the Accounting Trail
Financial Statements: Summarising data into the Trading Account, Profit & Loss Account, and Balance Sheet.
Significance of the Accounting Trail & Business Discipline
Verification: Allows every aggregated figure (e.g., Rs 5,00,000 total purchases) to be verified against raw purchase invoices.
Significance of the Accounting Trail & Business Discipline
Internal Control: Minimises fraud, unauthorised entries, duplications, omissions, and record manipulation.
Significance of the Accounting Trail & Business Discipline
Auditability: Facilitates statutory and internal audits by allowing auditors to verify every step of document processing.
Significance of the Accounting Trail & Business Discipline
Process Discipline: Demonstrates that accounting is an integrated system where transaction recording requires systematic completion.
Significance of the Accounting Trail & Business Discipline
Dispute Resolution: Provides clear evidentiary records to settle account discrepancies with suppliers or clients.
Transaction: Goods worth Rs 12,000 purchased on credit from M/s Shakti Suppliers.

Step-by-Step Path: a. Source Document: Purchase Invoice received from M/s Shakti Suppliers. b. Analysis: Identified as a credit purchase affecting Purchases A/c and Shakti Suppliers A/c. c. Journal Entry: Purchases A/c Dr. 12,000 / To Shakti Suppliers A/c 12,000. d. Ledger Posting: Debited to Purchases A/c; Credited to Shakti Suppliers A/c. e. Trial Balance: Included in the debit balance of Purchases and credit balance of Shakti Suppliers. Financial Statements: Purchases linked to Trading Account; unpaid liability f. to Shakti Suppliers reported under Current Liabilities in the Balance Sheet.

modules.title: Transactions and Events
text: Transaction: A specific financial activity or dealing measurable in monetary terms that directly alters the financial position of a business.; External Transactions: Business interactions with external parties (e.g., buying goods from vendors, selling services to customers, paying bank interest).; Internal Transactions: Financial adjustments occurring entirely within the entity (e.g., charging depreciation, writing off bad debts).

Event: Any occurrence or happening connected to a business. Every transaction is an event, but not every event is an accounting transaction.; Recordable Accounting Events: Occurrences with measurable monetary impacts on assets, liabilities, expenses, or equity (e.g., inventory lost in a fire, machinery depreciation).; Non-Recordable Events: Occurrences lacking precise monetary measurement (e.g., hiring a key executive, changes in management, market rumours, staff morale shifts).
Meaning - Transaction: A specific financial dealing affecting the business entity; Event: A broader occurrence or outcome related to the business.
Monetary Measurability - Transaction: Must be objectively measurable in monetary terms; Event: Required only if it is to be recorded in accounting books.
Recording - Transaction: Always recorded in accounting records; Event: Recorded only when it produces a measurable financial effect.
Examples - Transaction: Purchase of goods, payment of rent, cash sales; Event: Stock destruction by fire, machinery depreciation, obsolescence.
Four Characteristics of an Accounting Transaction
An event must meet all four criteria to be recognized as an accounting transaction:
Four Characteristics of an Accounting Transaction
Relates to the Business Entity: Must pertain to the business rather than the owner's personal affairs (though personal funds introduced or withdrawn by the owner qualify as Capital/Drawings).
Four Characteristics of an Accounting Transaction
Measurable in Money: Must be capable of clear, objective monetary evaluation.
Four Characteristics of an Accounting Transaction
Affects Financial Position: Must alter assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, or expenses.
Four Characteristics of an Accounting Transaction
Supported by Source Evidence: Must be verifiable via document proof (e.g., bills, receipts) or internal calculations (e.g., depreciation schedules).
